slides.title: Dissecting The Questions
text: Look at the last sentence in the question
Strategy words: first, priority, next, immediate, last, most (will be bolded)

slides.title: Test Taking Strategies
text: Avoid asking yourself - well, what if, but, and I assume
Always use the process of elimination when choices or options are presented
Use all your nursing knowledge, correct clinical experiences, and your test-taking skills and strategies to answer the question
Confidence in your ability to make a correct choice. You know this information
Decrease anxiety by taking relaxing deep breaths, breaks, and come prepared
Remember the Scope of Practice (nationally, not hospital/state specific)

slides.title: More Strategies
text: If the question asks you what to do in a situation
Use the nursing process to determine which step is next
If the question asks what the client needs
Use Maslow's Hierarchy to determine what to do first
Always choose the physical answer before the psychological answer
Use unless a safety concern such as suicidal thoughts
If the question involves communicating with a client
Use the principles of therapeutic communication
Prioritize what actions the nurse should take first
Consider life threatening complication at the same time as an in-service, or a client awaiting discharge, elective surgical procedure

slides.title: Who’s going to die?
text: When in distress, do NOT assess, except on 3rd party report.

slides.title: Multiple Choice Example:The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. Which of the following clients should the nurse see first?
text: Multiple Choice Example:The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. Which of the following clients should the nurse see first?
Client with a spinal cord injury who is flushed, diaphoretic.
Client with diabetes mellitus (type 2) who has a finger stick glucose level of 242 mg/dL.
Client with hyperparathyroidism with a calcium level of 11.5 mg/dL.
Client with angina complaining of a headache after receiving prescribed nitroglycerin.

slides.title: Multiple Choice Example:The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. The UAP reports that a client is complaining of chest pain. Which of the following actions should the nurse perform first?
text: Multiple Choice Example:The nurse is caring for a group of assigned clients on the medical surgical unit. The UAP reports that a client is complaining of chest pain. Which of the following actions should the nurse perform first?
Ask the UAP to get a complete set of vital signs on the client.

slides.title: NGN: NCLEX Multiple Response
text: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is talking with a 42-year-old client who has hypertension and is receiving a loop diuretic. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
“I should still follow my low-sodium diet.”
“I will stand slowly from a seated position.”
“I will increase my fluid intake each day to 5L.”
“I should weight myself once a month.”
“I will take the medication at the same time of the day, every day.”

slides.title: NGN: Cloze/Drop Down
text: The nurse in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a 9-year-old client with asthma. Parent at bedside. Client reports chest tightness with cough especially at night for the past 2 evenings. Expiratory wheeze auscultated throughout the chest. Vital signs: T 98.6 °F (37°C), P 110, RR 28, pulse oximetry reading 89% on room air. Sitting in tripod position with arms draped over bedside table. Complete the following sentence by choosing from the list of options.
apply humidified supplemental oxygen at 2L/min via nasal cannula
ask parent about allergens in the home
remind the client how to use metered dose inhaler
check the client’s peak flow with a peak expiratory flow meter

slides.title: NGN: Drag and drop Cloze

The nurse in the emergency department (ED) is caring for a 90-year-old client with acute onset confusion. The family states that the client has not been drinking water often and has a history of being immobilized in bed Vital signs: T 101.3 °F (38.5°C), P 120, RR 28, Blood pressure of 80/50 mmHg. Complete the following sentence by choosing from the list of options.
The nurse should recognize that the client may be experiencing ________, _________, and ________.

slides.title: NGN: Bow-Tie Item (part one)
text: The nurse in the inpatient psychiatric unit is caring for a 35-year-old client.

1000: Admitted to the unit directly from the emergency department (ED) stating, “I just can't take it anymore, the ups and downs are killing me!" “My actions have destroyed my life, the gambling, the spending, and now the lows have happened again. I hate myself" Hair is unwashed. Affect and mood are congruent. Client and spouse cannot confirm or deny compliance with prescribed medications. Spouse reports inability to locate prescriptions pill bottles in the home. Personal belongings searched in the presence of client, spouse, and security representative. Belongings are negative for contraband.

1200: Smiling and laughing the client states “Can I run a workout program for everyone on the unit? I think that I can reorganize the entire unit! ." the client is excitable and is walking back and forth in the room. Prescription medications are confirmed with client’s pharmacy and administered. Checked oral cavity and confirmed client swallowed prescribed doses of fluoxetine HCL, buspirone HCL, and oxcarbazepine. Spouse left the unit and plans to bring more clothes for the client later this evening.
0800: The client has slept through breakfast and is crying in bed.

slides.title: NGN: Highlight Text or Table Example
text: NGN: Highlight Text or Table Example
Directions: Highlight the findings below that would indicate the client is not progressing as expected

Client is post-operative day # 4 after an appendectomy and can ambulate in the corridor 2 times a day with minimal assistance. The client has a Jackson-Pratt (JP) drain noted with minimal drainage of 15mL/ day. The client is refusing to use the incentive spirometer stating it causes too much pain. The client is taking the prescribed client-controlled analgesia (PCA) device as ordered. The client states they are not experiencing nausea or vomiting. The abdominal surgical incision site with dressing is clean, dry, and intact. There is noted redness and edema at the incision site.

slides.title: NGN: Matrix Multiple Choice
text: The nurse in the outpatient clinic is caring for a 40-year-old client that is taking an ACE inhibitor.
For each action listed, click to specify if the action is indicated or not indicated for the client.
Teach the client to report if a dry cough occurs
Teach the client that the medication should be taken without food.
Advise the client to increase potassium intake.
Female clients who become pregnant should immediately notify the provider.
